_source: docs/07 §10.3's five writing rules and its sample log block; docs/14 §5.3.5's `log_templates` field and §5.4 assertion 7; presented per docs/13 §11.1's italic quoted joke line under the mistake header.
_notes: THE FIVE WRITING RULES, docs/07 §10.3, verbatim. Every line in this file answers to them and a human read against them is the ship gate (docs/16 R-3):
1. One sentence. The joke is in the sentence, not in a paragraph.
2. The raider is a person with a reason, not a random number generator. 'Greg saw a big number' beats 'Greg made an error'.
3. Never explain the mechanic in the joke line — the mechanical effect is already on the structured entry and tier 2 shows the math.

4. Each mistake type needs at least 6 template variants so a long raid does not repeat. Legendary raiders get their own variants, because a named legendary failing is inherently funnier than Steve failing.
5. Never blame the player. The player is the guild leader reading a report; the comedy is affectionate exasperation, not scolding.

TOKEN CONTRACT. `{actor}` is the ONLY substitution token, because it is the only field a `Mistakes.MistakeEvent` can resolve — the event carries `actor_id`, type, severity, round and cascade, and NO target. docs/07 §10.3's own sample line 'Cindy heals Natsuna…' names a second person, and that name is unresolvable here; it is adapted rather than copied. A `{target}` or `{tank}` token would be a crash waiting for a specific fight, so `MistakeLines._check_tokens` rejects every token but `{actor}`.

RULES 1 AND 4 AS MACHINE CHECKS. The envelope is taken from docs/07 §10.3's own sample block rather than from a preference: the sample's 'Bob assumed someone else was handling it. Bob was the someone else.' is two sentences and names the raider twice, so the checkable form of rule 1 is at most two sentences and one-or-two `{actor}` tokens. Length is capped at twice docs/13 §11.1's 74-character measure. Both constants live in `sim/content/MistakeLines.gd`; see `build/plan/q-comedy.md`.

RULE 3 AS A MACHINE CHECK. Banned substrings, case-insensitive: 'threat', 'hp', 'dps', 'cooldown', 'mitigat', '%'. A line that reaches for one of those is explaining the mechanic that tier 2 already prints.

BUDGET. docs/07 §10.3 rule 4 and docs/14 §5.4 assertion 7 both say >= 6. The shipped goldens fire one type up to 12 times inside a single encounter (Forgot to Taunt, e1_commons_starting, 22 rounds), so six repeats verbatim twice in a raid the player watches tonight. Eight measured-hot types carry 14 variants and the other ten carry 8. The floor of 6 is still enforced, on the UNGATED subset of every type, so a class gate can only ever add.

OPTIONAL KEYS. `severity` and `classes` are absent on an unrestricted variant, which means 'any'; `null` and `[]` mean the same thing and both load. A gate is an EXTRA on top of the floor, never part of it.

LEGENDARY VARIANTS live in this file, not in `data/legendaries/*.json` — the reasoning, and the counter-argument from `dialogue_barks`, are in `build/plan/q-comedy.md`. Eight of the nine legendaries are deliberately nameless (docs/03 §5.6: 'DO NOT INVENT NAMES'), so every line here uses `{actor}` and no line contains a proper noun; `MistakeLines._check_capitals` enforces that.

NOT CERTIFIED FUNNY. docs/16 R-3 makes 'is reading it entertaining' the question the whole game is gated on and says nothing in the doc set can prove it. The validators prove shape, coverage and non-repetition. They do not prove rule 2 or rule 5. This corpus needs a human read before the backlog item is done.
